vendor: Engineering in the Age of AI (eai-org)
tagline: Refine → Plan → Act → Consolidate: a fresh session per phase, handing over a file.
bestFor: Ticket-driven work with a human reviewing each step

phases.label: Ticket
phases.note: Downloads the ticket from a tracker (Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps…) into a self-contained TICKET.md, with attachments and linked tickets. No tracker: write the file by hand, or start Refine from a raw idea.

phases.label: Refine
phases.note: **The what.** Checks the ticket against the codebase and interviews you one question at a time, each with a recommended answer. Output: a validated REQUIREMENTS.md.

phases.label: Harden reqs (optional)
phases.note: Optional, in a fresh session. A clean-context sub-agent reviews REQUIREMENTS.md against the ticket, code, and related tickets; your session tries to disprove each finding, and you decide on the survivors: fix, dismiss, or defer.

phases.label: Plan
phases.note: **The how.** Studies the code, settles technical decisions with you, and writes a self-contained PLAN.md for a fresh session to execute.

phases.label: Harden plan (optional)
phases.note: Optional, in a fresh session. The same adversarial review as for requirements, applied to PLAN.md.

phases.label: Split tasks (optional)
phases.note: Optional. Breaks PLAN.md into small tasks, each leaving the project building with passing tests, grouped into PR-sized batches. After you approve, it appends the list to the plan, with a done check and a suggested commit subject per task.

phases.label: Act
phases.note: **One task per fresh session.** Implements only that task, runs its done check and the project's checks, ticks it off in PLAN.md, and logs deviations in DECISIONS.md. It never commits or pushes. A second failed attempt, or a task that needs reshaping, stops the run to re-plan. An unsplit plan needs no skill: ask a fresh session to execute PLAN.md.

phases.label: Review task
phases.note: **The review between tasks is the point.** You check the result and commit it, then start the next task in a fresh session. A finished PR-sized group moves on to Consolidate.

phases.label: Consolidate: review
phases.note: **Consolidate, step one.** A clean-context sub-agent reviews the changeset and reports its findings back to your session. /self-review builds on it for a merge-ready pass, with a compact report for the PR.

phases.label: Consolidate: handover
phases.note: **Consolidate, step two.** Writes HANDOVER.md, a paste-ready PR description covering key decisions, where to look, and open items. If the repo has a PR template, it fills that in instead.

scenarios.note: The toolkit says trivial, well-defined tasks **may skip phases**, and nothing enforces the flow, so a one-liner goes straight to Act.
The full path suits a large feature: **code-checked requirements, a hardened plan, and PR-sized groups**. The cost is that each task is a separate manual run.
Refine checks claims against the real code and split keeps the project building after every task, which suits **multi-file changes in small reviewable steps**.
**No hotfix path.** The interview and fresh-session handoffs are slow when production is down, and skipping them gives up what the pattern adds.
Groups are independently mergeable, but there is **no worktree isolation or orchestration**. Each team runs its own flow and coordinates by hand.
The plan can list every form and split tracks each one, but **one task per run** means many manual runs unless forms are batched into a task.

keyFeatures: Each phase runs in a fresh session and hands over a file, not chat history: TICKET.md → REQUIREMENTS.md → PLAN.md → HANDOVER.md
Refine interviews you one question at a time; in both Refine and Plan, anything the code can answer is settled by reading the code
Optional /harden-artifact: a clean-context reviewer tests a requirements doc or plan, then your session tries to disprove each finding
/split-plan-tasks and /execute-plan-tasks run one small task per session and stop for your review; the agent never commits or pushes
Consolidate: /fresh-eyes-review by a clean-context sub-agent, then /handover writes a paste-ready PR description
Starts from a tracker ticket or a raw idea; works with Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, OpenCode, and others
MIT, ~80 stars; take the whole toolkit or only the skills you want
limitations: A skill collection, not a framework: nothing enforces the flow, and each phase is invoked by hand
One task per run: long plans need many manual invocations
Requirements and plans are per-task working files — no maintained living spec
No worktree isolation or parallel multi-agent orchestration
Young project with no tagged releases; skills change often
Scores assessed from the repository and docs on 2026-11-04 by an agent-toolkit contributor, so not an independent review
